Observed report and runtime:
- Gerrit change 986 patchset 1 is NEW at revision d51c056d0b4859d1a5fcb311b311c4e531919078. Public Gerrit REST records LLM-Review +1 by rebar-review-bot at 2026-07-27 22:58:53 UTC, zero unresolved comments, and the commit message contains `rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d`. `/review/health` returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

- The newest Gerrit-shaped artifact (`code-review: I… @ <revision>`) was created at 1783832480571739905; no later live Gerrit artifact is present, although local `session:` artifacts continue.

Repository and history:
- `voter.py:730` calls `emit_code_review_artifact(..., repo_root=None)` only after a confirmed vote. The emitter creates/reuses the artifact, emits the v2 sidecar, resolves trailers, and swallows any outer exception while emitting `ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR` (`voter.py:260-367`).
- Commit d09e9c35c added `infra/scripts/reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh`, installs/calls it from `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, and tests that a fresh tickets clone gains repo-local identity plus `.env-id`; it also added the greppable error marker.
- Commit 79a10387a added compose `GIT_CONFIG_*` safe.directory for `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` after live logs proved persistent-volume ownership blocked all artifact writes. Ticket a698 records a successful 2026-07-16 redeploy and zero markers after deploy, but explicitly says no fresh vote occurred, so end-to-end artifact creation was not observed.
- Current compose sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always`, the safe.directory override, and the named persistent volume. Current origin/main is dcc90ced4 and the debug worktree is clean at that SHA.

Access/unknowns:
- The production host is SSM-only in AWS account 896586841071. Available CLI credentials resolve to accounts 820258254566 and 579718921998, so host journald/container inspection is not currently possible. Exact `ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR` text, deployed SHA, container env, volume state, ensure output, and tracker git state remain unknown.

rebar-debug Phase 1 exit (2026-07-27):

Blind-investigator fishbone:
- Code logic: `push_tickets_branch` always returns None and swallows publication failures (`src/rebar/_store/push.py:108-174`); `emit_code_review_artifact` therefore returns a local artifact id as apparent success (`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:260-367`). After the external vote, the voter records dedup before artifact emission (`voter.py:703-737`); both the local-dedup and Gerrit-existing-vote guards return before any artifact work (`voter.py:513-543`).
- State/config/environment candidates (invalid PAT, write-dead clone, ownership, recovery state, ambient-store misrouting) can initiate the persistence failure, but all funnel into the same non-recoverable state-machine defect. Sidecar-only failure would leave a visible CREATE and is not needed to explain total absence.

Discriminating runtime proof:
1. An initialized ephemeral tracker was wired to a rejecting remote and driven through the real emitter. The emitter returned a code_review id; the local artifact, REVIEW_RESULT commits, and relates_to link existed; the remote contained zero revision commits; no ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR marker was emitted. This confirms silent local-only success and rules out verdict/trailer/bootstrap failure for that mechanism.
2. The real review entry point was instrumented on retry. With either a recorded dedup row or an existing Gerrit vote, it returned `dedup` / `already_voted_gerrit` and invoked the artifact emitter zero times. This confirms the failed artifact cannot self-heal on ordinary webhook/reconciler delivery.
3. The write-dead-store regression produced None plus ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR, distinguishing bootstrap/write failure. Forcing sidecar.emit=False produced a CREATE-only artifact and no outer marker, distinguishing the inner-swallow alternative. Focused artifact coverage remained green (21 tests; the code-trace investigator independently ran 25 focused tests).

Proven root cause: the review-bot ledger models only “vote completed,” not “artifact durably persisted.” Artifact work occurs after that irreversible state, the publish API cannot report durability failure, and both normal retry guards suppress recovery. Consequently any post-vote store/publish fault can leave a healthy +1 vote with no shared artifact forever. This one mechanism explains the live vote, missing shared ticket/link/payload, healthy process, absent publish-specific marker, and persistence across retries.

Legitimacy: DEFECT. Story ef70-e108-e6d4-4d7c and `voter.py:269-274` require one durable revision-scoped artifact per completed review; dogfood story 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d authoritatively requires its ambient-store v2 trace.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is that votes remain non-blocking while artifact durability is explicitly observable and incomplete artifacts remain recoverable. The emitter has one production caller. Generic push callers rely on best-effort/no-raise, so that existing API must remain unchanged; artifact-specific reporting/recovery can be added without a behavioral dependency conflict. Dedup/reconciler callers rely only on preventing duplicate votes, not on suppressing missing-artifact repair. Phase 2 is unlocked.

Phase 2 frozen test contract card:
- authoritative_contract: story ef70-e108-e6d4-4d7c and bug ACs require a durable shared revision-scoped code_review artifact, v2 payload, relates_to link, non-blocking vote, and actionable bounded failure diagnostics.
- trigger_preconditions: real initialized local tickets clone; real bare origin seeded with cited work; origin then made unreachable during the first post-vote artifact write; confirmed local artifact/ahead state and one successful Gerrit vote.
- production_path: `review_and_vote` -> real emitter -> real append/commit -> real git push -> dedup retry guard. Gerrit network and LLM are the only stateful fakes.
- test_tier: stateful contract/integration test with real temporary Git repositories. A function-level unit test is insufficient because the defect is local-vs-remote reachability plus retry state.
- observable_postcondition: first vote remains successful and singular; failure emits ARTIFACT_EMIT_ERROR stage=publish; after the same ordinary delivery is retried with origin restored, exactly one artifact, its v2 payload, and its relates_to link are visible from a fresh remote clone, without a second vote.
- ci_gate: pytest exact node; make test / CI unit suite.
- negative_control: a third delivery while already synchronized creates no vote, artifact, or remote commit.
- collateral_invariants: cited work remains present; local tracker clean; idempotent artifact count one.
- recovery: clean retry after transport restoration publishes the pending artifact.
- fault_injection: replace the real tracker origin URL with a nonexistent local bare-repo path at the actual git-push boundary, then restore it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Correction after experimental root-cause proof and production recovery (2026-07-28):

The earlier Phase 1 account correctly described why an artifact failure could persist, but it did not identify the initiating persistence failure. Real two-clone experiments isolated that cause. Enrichment queue pruning physically deleted committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, and DONE_ENRICH events; digest keep=1 pruning physically deleted committed TICKET_DIGEST events. Queue deletion alone reproduced stale-clone merge conflicts on DONE_ENRICH. Digest deletion alone reproduced conflicts on TICKET_DIGEST. With both deletion paths disabled, the same independently advancing clones merged cleanly and retained the union of both histories. Production recovery then reproduced exactly two DONE_ENRICH rename/delete conflicts at the frozen divergent tips. Therefore destructive event deletion created the unreconcilable tracker divergence; vote/dedup retry suppression was only an amplifier that prevented self-healing after persistence failed.

Recovery preserved and republished the original revision artifact 8172-4554-a9fc-47da. After the repair deployed and the tracker reconverged, a forced rerun of Gerrit change 986 created fresh shared artifact a4b7-f176-50af-49aa with schema code_review_result_v2 and a relates_to link from work ticket 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d. The tracker remained clean and 0 ahead / 0 behind.

This ticket remains open: revision d51c056d0b4859d1a5fcb311b311c4e531919078 now has two revision-scoped artifacts (8172-4554-a9fc-47da and a4b7-f176-50af-49aa), so the acceptance criterion requiring exactly one idempotent artifact is not yet met. Resolving that duplicate/idempotency defect remains in this ticket scope.

comments.body: rebar-debug Phase 1 residual-defect proof (2026-07-28): three independent code-trace, historical, and empirical lenses converged. Manual /rerun reconstructs the Gerrit event with REST ChangeInfo.id (`rebar~986`), while the live webhook supplied canonical Change-Id (`I969fce55bf212e539f67009ff42447fb234068df`). `_extract` preserves either raw string; `emit_code_review_artifact` uses it in the fingerprint and exact title key. A sequential local real-store experiment with the same decision/diff/revision reused an artifact for the identical raw id but created a second for the alternate id (count 1→2); repeating the alternate id reused the second. This rules out lookup failure, store visibility, revision drift, concurrency, and tracker divergence as causes of the duplicate. History shows the mismatch entered with rerun commit 514ffa054 and exact-title artifact identity 10837ca88; no fix exists on any ref. DEFECT authority: this ticket requires exactly one idempotent revision-scoped artifact. Phase 2 is unlocked. Existing artifacts 8172-4554-a9fc-47da (canonical I… title, incomplete/orphaned) and a4b7-f176-50af-49aa (compact rebar~986 title, linked v2 recovery artifact) require an explicit data-reconciliation decision after code repair.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

The live dogfood probe on Gerrit change 986 patchset 1 (revision d51c056d0b4859d1a5fcb311b311c4e531919078) received LLM-Review +1 at 2026-07-27 22:58:53 UTC with zero unresolved comments, proving the deployed reviewer ran. The commit contains `rebar-ticket: 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d`. However, the best-effort Gerrit voter persistence seam did not produce the required durable artifact: after a ticket write reconciled the shared tracker, `rebar search` found neither the revision nor Change-Id and `rebar audit show 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d --output json | jq .code_reviews` remained empty.

## Plan

- Reproduce and trace `review_bot.voter.emit_code_review_artifact` in the deployed Gerrit path, including tracker initialization/sync, exception observability, artifact creation, sidecar emission, and `relates_to` trailer resolution.
- Identify the precise changeable cause rather than treating best-effort swallowing as sufficient.
- Add a RED regression at the smallest real voter/tracker boundary, implement the fix, and retain fail-safe voting behavior plus actionable emission diagnostics.
- Land through Gerrit, allow deployment, and rerun the live change-986 dogfood revision to prove a `code_review_result_v2` artifact is persisted and linked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A live Gerrit review with a resolvable `rebar-ticket:` trailer persists one idempotent revision-scoped `code_review` artifact and links it `relates_to` the work ticket.
- [ ] The persisted `code_review_result_v2` payload exposes `coverage.llm_ran` and the blocking/advisory/dropped/indeterminate data needed by the dogfood comparison.
- [ ] Artifact persistence failures remain non-blocking for the vote but emit actionable bounded diagnostics identifying the failed stage.
- [ ] Automated coverage reproduces the failure before the fix and passes after it without weakening existing voter tests.
- [ ] The change lands via Gerrit with LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, and zero unresolved comments; the live dogfood probe then observes the artifact.
